display.purpose: Hero metrics — big numbers that anchor progress screens. Used sparingly for key performance indicators.

headline.purpose: Screen titles and section headers. The primary structural type.

title.purpose: Card titles, list item headings. Dense but readable.

body.purpose: Primary text — descriptions, instructions, data values. Max line length 65–75ch for prose.

label.purpose: Tags, badges, metadata, timestamps. Small but legible.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Default card state. Separates cards from the screen background.

shadows.name: card-elevated
shadows.purpose: Active or important cards. Same shadow, elevated surface color.

shadows.name: button-press
shadows.purpose: Primary button glow on press. Coral shadow creates tactile feedback.

motion.name: spring-press
motion.purpose: Scale-press animation for buttons and interactive elements.

motion.name: spring-release
motion.purpose: Scale-release animation returning to default state.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Main action button. Signal coral background, black text, pill shape, scale-press feedback.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #FF5A36; color: #000000; padding: 16px 24px; min-height: 56px; border-radius: 18px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.3px; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1), box-shadow 0.15s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: scale(1.02); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(255,90,54,0.28); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FF5A36; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Subtle Button
components.description: Secondary action button. Translucent background, white text, 1px border.
components.css: .ds-btn-subtle { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06); color: #FFFFFF; padding: 16px 24px; min-height: 56px; border-radius: 18px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.3px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-subtle:hover { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-color: rgba(255,255,255,0.12); } .ds-btn-subtle:active { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.10); } .ds-btn-subtle:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #FF5A36; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-subtle:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Default container. Mat black background, subtle border, generous rounding.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #0D0D0D; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius: 24px; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); }

components.name: Elevated Card
components.description: Active or important card. Lighter surface, same shadow.
components.css: .ds-card-elevated { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.07); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); border-radius: 24px; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Text input. Translucent background, white text, coral focus ring.
components.css: .ds-input { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.04); color: #FFFFFF; padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 15px; transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: rgba(255,255,255,0.25); } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #FF5A36; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(255,90,54,0.2); } .ds-input:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Chip
components.description: Tag or filter chip. Translucent background, pill shape, muted text.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 8px 12px; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.06); color: rgba(255,255,255,0.45); border-radius: 999px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.4px; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-chip-selected { background: #FF5A36; color: #000000; }

components.name: Metric Block
components.description: Large-format data display for progress screens. Display/headline weight numbers with muted labels.
components.css: .ds-metric { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; } .ds-metric-value { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 40px; font-weight: 700; color: #FFFFFF; line-height: 48px; } .ds-metric-label { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.45); letter-spacing: 0.4px; text-transform: uppercase; }

narrative.overview:
Athelix treats the interface like a precision instrument — raw, functional, stripped to essentials. The dark palette isn't aesthetic decoration; it's practical for gym environments where overhead fluorescents glare off bright screens. Every element earns its place like equipment in a well-organized weight room: nothing decorative, everything functional. The visual language draws from the confidence of a training log that's seen real progress — precise data, clear hierarchy, no hesitation.

The system rejects the generic fitness app aesthetic: no motivational quotes, no social feeds, no lifestyle photography. It also rejects clinical interfaces that feel like medical dashboards. Athelix lives in the space between — empowering data for healthy people training hard, not diagnostic readouts for patients.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first for gym environments (reduced glare, focus on content)
Translucent layering over shadows for depth
Single accent color (coral) for primary actions only

rules.name: The Coral Restraint Rule
rules.body: Signal coral appears on primary actions and active states only. Never for decoration, never for large surfaces, never for secondary elements. Its rarity creates hierarchy; overuse destroys it.

rules.name: The Translucent Layer Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from stacking translucent white layers, not from shadows. Cards, inputs, and containers use rgba(255,255,255,0.04–0.07) to create separation. Shadows appear only as state feedback (press, elevation).

rules.name: The Metric Scale Rule
rules.body: Large numbers (progress values, percentages, personal records) use the display/headline weights at scale. They are the visual anchors of their screens — confident, unmissable, data-forward.

rules.name: The No-Display-Font Rule
rules.body: System fonts only. No custom typefaces for headings, no decorative fonts for labels. The interface disappears into the task; the typography never calls attention to itself.

rules.name: The Ambient Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows are diffuse and ambient, never sharp. They create gentle separation between layers, not dramatic lifting. The shadow under a card should feel like soft ambient light, not a spotlight.

rules.name: The State-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows appear at rest for structural separation (cards, modals) and intensify for state feedback (press, hover). Shadows never appear purely for decoration.

dos: Do use the coral accent sparingly — primary actions and active states only, ≤10% of screen surface.
Do use translucent layering (rgba white tints) for depth instead of heavy shadows.
Do keep system fonts for all text — the interface should feel native to each platform.
Do use skeleton states for loading, not spinners in the middle of content.
Do ensure touch targets are 44×44pt minimum (iOS) / 48×48dp minimum (Android) for sweaty fingers.
Do test contrast under bright gym lighting — high-contrast data is non-negotiable.
Do use scale-press feedback on all interactive elements for tactile confidence.
Do keep one task per screen — focused interfaces beat feature-packed dashboards.
donts: Don't use generic fitness app aesthetics: motivational quotes, social feeds, lifestyle photography, "great job!" cheerleading. Athelix is a tool, not a content platform.
Don't use clinical/medical aesthetics: diagnostic dashboards, white-coat vibes, rehab app patterns. The data should feel empowering, not diagnostic.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism as default, or decorative motion that doesn't convey state.
Don't use display fonts for UI labels, buttons, or data — system fonts only.
Don't stack FABs or use modals as first thought — exhaust inline alternatives first.
Don't reinvent standard affordances for flavor — use platform-native controls (iOS switches, Android Material components).
Don't use border-left greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe — use full borders or background tints.
Don't ship with missing component states — every interactive element needs default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error.
